land.text: the Muslim lands of the South Caucasus, proclaimed independent by the Azerbaijani National Council 'after the Transcaucasian federation fell' on 28 May 1918

predecessors.note: The infobox lists the Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic as predecessor; no dossier or Cliopatria row exists for it.

land.text: the republic 'occupied' by the Soviet 11th Army on 28 April 1920

successors.note: Infobox successor: Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic.

capitals.name: Ganja
capitals.note: Infobox 'Ganja (until September 1918)'; the page gives no start date for Ganja.

capitals.name: Baku
capitals.note: 'Baku became capital in September 1918' (the Ottoman Army of Islam entered Baku on 15 September 1918).

keyframe_review.note: 87,458 km2 against the infobox's 99,908.87 km2 for 1918: a ratio of 0.88. The shape (44.8-50.3 E, 38.5-41.8 N) takes in Nakhichevan, Zangezur and a strip south of the Aras, all claimed from Armenia (and Iran) rather than held; the page warns that 'the map of the ADR does not show disputed territories'. Kept as the claimed extent, with the contests in the ledger.

72,209 km2, 0.72 of the infobox 99,909 km2. The shape stops at 45.4 E, leaving out Nakhichevan and Zangezur, where Armenian forces took Nakhichevan city in June 1919 (retaken in July) and held 'the Armenian-controlled section of Zangezur' (war page). It keeps Karabakh, disputed with Armenia, and the Lankaran/Mughan district, which a 'Mughan Soviet Republic' held from 15 May 1919.

correction.text: the 1919 shape carried to 1920: the republic that 'ceased to exist on 28 April 1920' when the Soviet 11th Army occupied it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, years only: Cliopatria stops in 1919; the republic lasted to 28 April 1920. Karabakh was in dispute (fighting 'intensified by February 1920', martial law in Karabakh) and the March 1920 Shusha events are on the war page.

region.text: the Muslim South Caucasus, 'Independence declared: 28 May 1918'

ledger.note: 28 May 1918: the Azerbaijani National Council proclaims independence after the Transcaucasian federation falls. The page gives the date and the predecessor but no frontier; the shape is Cliopatria's claimed extent. The Treaty of Batum with the Ottoman Empire, the republic's first treaty, is undated on this page (4 June 1918 on the First Republic of Armenia page).

region.text: Baku, entered on 15 September 1918 by the Ottoman Army of Islam with Azeri allies after 'Dunsterville ordered the evacuation on 14 September 1918'

ledger.note: 15 September 1918: 'The Ottoman Army of Islam and its Azeri allies, led by Nuri Pasha, entered Baku on 15 September'; the republic's government makes it the capital. Baku's government until then was the 'Centro Caspian Dictatorship (1 August 1918 – 15 September 1918)', which 'was supported by the British' (Dunsterville). Reviewer eu-19-f: counterpart was a description ('Baku defenders (Dunsterforce and the Centrocaspian Dictatorship)'); the Centrocaspian Dictatorship has no dossier yet.
September 1918: the capital moves from Ganja to Baku. 'Ganja (until September 1918)'.

region.text: Baku, where 'Allied troops arrived ... on 17 November 1918'

ledger.note: 17 November 1918: Allied (British) troops arrive in Baku after the Armistice of Mudros (30 October) replaced the Turkish troops. The page gives the Allies, not the extent beyond Baku, which is my reading.

region.text: Nagorno-Karabakh, seized by 'Armenian forces under Andranik' after Mudros, and Zangezur

ledger.note: Late 1918: Andranik's Armenians seize Karabakh. The war page gives no month or year for the seizure and none for the British appointment of Khosrov bey Sultanov as governor-general of Karabakh and Zangezur; November is a placement, not a date.

region.text: the Lankaran district, where the Mughan administration was overthrown on 25 April 1919 and the Mughan Soviet Republic proclaimed on 15 May 1919

ledger.note: 15 May 1919: the Mughan Soviet Republic is proclaimed in the Lankaran district after a pro-Bolshevik protest overthrew the Mughan administration on 25 April. The page does not say how or when it ended.

region.text: Nakhichevan, where 'Azerbaijani rebels' had declared the Republic of Aras in December 1918 and Armenian troops 'managed to capture the city of Nakhichevan in June 1919'

ledger.note: June 1919: Armenian troops under Drastamat Kanayan take Nakhichevan city and destroy the Republic of Aras; Azerbaijani and Ottoman troops retake it in July.
10 August 1919: ceasefire over Nakhichevan ('On 10 August 1919, a ceasefire was signed'); the dispute itself continued to 1920.
19 August 1919: 'British forces left' Baku, ending the Allied occupation that began on 17 November 1918.

28 April 1920: the republic ceases to exist, ending its contest with Armenia over Karabakh, Zangezur and Nakhichevan. The war page continues with Soviet Azerbaijan: Karabakh conquered by the Soviet 11th Army in May 1920, Zangezur ceded to Armenia in November 1920, Nakhichevan under Azerbaijan's protectorate by the Treaty of Moscow (16 March 1921).
1920: page silent on the Mughan Soviet Republic's end; the dossier closes the contest at the republic's own end, 28 April 1920, as a bridging judgment.

region.text: the republic occupied by the Soviet 11th Army

ledger.note: 28 April 1920: the Soviet 11th Army occupies the republic and it 'ceased to exist'. The operation began on 25 April and a Provisional Revolutionary Committee issued an ultimatum on 27 April.

wars.name: Armenian-Azerbaijani war (1918-1920)
wars.outcome: Inconclusive (30 March 1918 - 28 November 1920): 'Most of Zangezur gained by Soviet Armenia'; the Karabakh and Nakhichevan disputes settled for Soviet Azerbaijan. The republic held Karabakh until the Soviet takeover of April 1920; Azerbaijan's attack on Zangezur on 3 November 1919 was repulsed.
wars.note: The page puts the largest escalation in mid-March 1920 at Shusha. Armenian forces still held most of western Azerbaijan, including Karabakh and Nakhichevan, at the end of April 1920.

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Azerbaijan (April 1920)
wars.outcome: The operation began on 25 April; on 27 April a Provisional Revolutionary Committee issued an ultimatum; the 11th Army occupied the republic on 28 April and it ceased to exist.
wars.note: No fighting is described on the page; the government surrendered.

certainty.note: Frontiers with Armenia (Karabakh, Zangezur, Nakhichevan), Georgia (Balakan, Zaqatala, Qakh) and the North Caucasus (Derbent) were claims and contests; the page says the map of the republic does not show disputed territories.

notes:
Azerbaijan and Republic of Azerbaijan: Cliopatria's two rows share Wikidata Q227 and the Wikipedia title 'Azerbaijan', but they are different states: the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic (28 May 1918 - 28 April 1920, this dossier), the Azerbaijan SSR (azerbaijan-soviet-socialist-republic) and the Republic of Azerbaijan from 1991 (republic-of-azerbaijan, Cliopatria 1992-2024, another agent). They are not merged. The Wikipedia field is set to 'Azerbaijan Democratic Republic'; Cliopatria's is 'Azerbaijan'.
Scope: Cliopatria stops in 1919, but the republic lasted to 28 April 1920; a one-year keyframe for 1920 extends it. No rulers list is given: the infobox lists five 'Leaders' (Rasulzade 1918, Khoyski 1918-1919, Topchubashov 1918-1920, Yusifbeyli 1919-1920, Hajinski 1920) without saying which post each held, and their terms overlap.
Not dated by the pages opened: the 22 August 1919 Karabakh agreement (the war page says only 'in August 1919'), the Zaqatala and Balakan disputes with Georgia, the Derbent claim, the end of the Mughan Soviet Republic, the Georgian defensive treaty of 16 June 1919 (territory not involved). The 1918 and 1919 shapes are claimed extents: Nakhichevan and Zangezur are in the 1918 shape although Armenia held much of them.
Counterparts: transcaucasian-democratic-federative-republic, a Mughan Soviet Republic (1919, rebel state holding land for under a year: not given a dossier because its end is unknown), Dunsterforce/Centrocaspian Dictatorship (Baku 1918), Soviet 11th Army (russian-soviet-federative-socialist-republic); british-colonial-empire (eu-11, the British occupation of Baku).
Page budget (2 of 2) spent on the republic's page and the war page; the First Republic of Armenia page was opened for the Armenia dossier and used here for one cross-check date.
